messages:
elaine.sales: Hey team — FjordBank legal just asked for a "compliance kit" for the POC: SOC 2 Type II summary, ISO certificate, a signed pen-test confirmation/letter, and a short statement on data handling. They want to kick off procurement next week. Can we confirm what we can provide and an ETA? :thinking:

mike.se: We can provide the SOC2 summary + ISO cert (public scan). Full SOC2 report behind NDA. For the pen-test letter we have a standard template but security needs to sign off on details/wording. ETA depends on security availability, but I can get draft to you in 48h.

sasha.security: Quick checklist from our side: 1) Can we get customer NDA or PO? 2) Which env is the POC running in (hosted vs dedicated)? 3) Any export-control or regulated-data flags? If no NDA, we can still provide the high-level artifacts and the generic pen-test confirmation letter (no vuln details).

ana.ae: @sasha.security they requested hosted API POC (no PHI) but procurement insists on a signed pen-test letter for vendor risk. They asked specifically for a statement that an independent pentest was completed in the last 12 months and whether remediation actions exist.

sasha.security: OK that’s doable. We have a pen-test letter template that reads: "Redwood Inference confirms that an independent penetration test was conducted on <date>. No critical vulnerabilities were found. Remediation actions for medium findings were completed on <date>." We will redact tester details if legal asks. I can paste the template and a sample signed wording below.

compliance-bot: Attached: /internal/compliance/pen_test_letter_template_v1.pdf (access: security,legal,sales)

elaine.sales: Thanks. Is a redacted version acceptable to procurement? They usually need the tester name on the letter or a signed attestation from a named security lead. If we need to add a signature, who signs?

sasha.security: We typically have the security manager sign. For external-facing procurement requests we can include the tester name unless NDAs prevent it. If they insist on tester identity, we can ask procurement to accept a signed attestation instead.

mike.se: For speed, I suggest sending: (a) SOC2 summary PDF, (b) ISO27001 cert (public link), (c) the pen-test letter template filled with dates and signed by security manager, and (d) an IP/data handling blurb. I can assemble the SOC2 summary and blurb today and attach.

elaine.sales: Can you drop a short email template I can send to FjordBank procurement? I’ll attach the docs and ask for NDA if they want the full report.

sasha.security: Sure — sample email (paste as-is):

```
Hi Sam —

Attached are the materials for the Redwood Inference POC: SOC 2 Type II summary (redacted), ISO27001 certificate, and our pen-test attestation letter signed by our Security Manager. We can provide the full SOC 2 report and pen-test technical findings under a mutual NDA or as part of the procurement review. Please confirm whether a redacted attestation meets your vendor risk requirements or if you need the tester name and full report.

Best,
Elaine (on behalf of Redwood Inference)
```

ana.ae: Perfect. FjordBank wants the signed letter by Thursday. Is that realistic?

sasha.security: If they need only the attestation (no tester PII) — yes, we can sign by Thu. If they require tester identity and test artifacts, we need an NDA and that adds a 3–5 business day delay.

elaine.sales: Great — I’ll send the attestation path first and request NDA if they push for full reports. Mike, can you attach the SOC2 summary + blurb today? I’ll send the outreach and loop in procurement. :thumbsup:

mike.se: On it, will drop the files in this thread within a couple hours.

elaine.sales: Thanks all — I’ll update once procurement replies.
